intent.description: Research, create, improve, migrate, validate, and optionally publish Codex-native skills from workflows, prompts, transcripts, documents, SOPs, scripts, notes, or existing skills. Use when a reusable Codex skill should be created or materially updated, when useful mechanisms must be preserved during identity or workflow adaptation, when trigger and output boundaries need evaluation, or when a skill needs Codex metadata, release gates, or installation verification. Exclude one-off summaries, translations, ordinary documentation, non-skill package publishing, and requests that explicitly should not become a skill.
intent.job_to_be_done: Preserve useful mechanisms and turn repeated workflows or existing skills into lean Codex-native skills with proportional research, validation, and optional release gates.
target_users: 朱雀 AI and Codex users who create and maintain reusable skills

routing_rules: Route by the frontmatter `description` before reading the body.
Once selected, act as the single skill-authoring authority. Do not invoke another creator unless the user explicitly requests a comparison or this skill cannot complete the task.
Keep audit, evaluation, and diagnosis requests read-only. Edit only for create, update, migrate, or package requests. Publish only after an explicit publish request.
Reject one-off summaries, translations, explanations, and brainstorming as skill candidates unless a stable repeated workflow is demonstrated.
Keep exactly one discoverable root `SKILL.md`. Name embedded examples `SKILL.example.md` and test fixtures `SKILL.fixture.md`.
For migration or rebranding, classify existing parts as `keep`, `adapt`, `remove`, or `add` before editing. Never equate debranding with deleting useful mechanisms.
Use the 朱雀 AI identity only for 朱雀 AI-owned or explicitly branded output. Do not inject social links, QR codes, profile assets, or naming prefixes without supplied source material.
creation_workflow: Decide whether the request represents a stable repeated job. If not, answer directly and create no skill.
For an existing Skill, inventory its useful mechanisms and classify them as `keep`, `adapt`, `remove`, or `add` before changing files.
Capture the recurring job, target users, real inputs, finished output, exclusions, permissions, existing assets, destination, brand scope, and publication intent.
Collect two or three realistic examples and at least one near-neighbor that should not trigger.
Research prior art when the design is new, material, public, or high-risk; otherwise record why it is unnecessary.
Plan only the reusable scripts, references, and assets earned by the examples.
For a new skill, run the bundled Codex initializer:
Replace all TODOs, remove unused placeholders and directories, and implement the smallest complete workflow.
Test every added script by running it. Test a representative sample only when many scripts are mechanically similar.
Run the official Codex quick validator and the extended project validator:
For Production or higher, add realistic should-trigger, should-not-trigger, and near-neighbor cases. Treat `trigger_eval.py` as static lint, not proof of real Codex activation.
Forward-test complex skills on realistic tasks with fresh context. Pass raw inputs and the skill, not the intended answer, diagnosis, or expected fix.
Add with-skill versus baseline output evaluation only when correctness, safety, persuasion, or repeatability justifies it.
Produce a concise handoff with preserved value, 朱雀 AI adaptations, reference skills studied, candidate-specific lessons, design advantages, validated advantages, hypotheses, and missing evidence.
evidence_rules: Static validation proves package shape, not output quality.
Recorded fixtures prove reproducibility, not provider-backed model performance.
Static trigger lint proves description/case alignment, not real Codex invocation accuracy.
Human blind review counts only when the reviewer, time, decision, rubric reason, and answer isolation are recorded.
Preview, generated files, successful commands, PR creation, merge, Release, and clean installation are distinct states.
output_contract: a working skill directory with one root `SKILL.md`
only the scripts, references, and assets needed by the workflow
validation results and any realistic test evidence
explicit missing evidence and permission boundaries

interface.short_description: Preserve value and create Codex-native skills
interface.default_prompt: Use $zhuque-skills-create to preserve what works and turn this repeated workflow into a lean, validated Codex skill.

evidence_boundary.public_claim_policy: claim only what local validation, install proof, human review, or provider-backed evidence actually supports
